definitions.explanation: A deciduous conifer native to the central Japanese mountains, distinctive for being one of the few Japanese conifers whose needles turn yellow and fall in autumn.

examples.japanese: {唐松|からまつ}の{林|はやし}を{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I walked through a larch forest.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると{唐松|からまつ}が{黄色|きいろ}くなる。
examples.english: In autumn, the larches turn yellow.

examples.japanese: {長野県|ながのけん}の{高原|こうげん}には{広大|こうだい}な{唐松|からまつ}の{植林地|しょくりんち}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
examples.english: On the highlands of Nagano Prefecture, vast larch plantations extend in every direction.

notes:
Also written {落葉松|からまつ} (literally "falling-leaf pine"), which reflects the fact that — unlike most conifers — the karamatsu sheds its needles each autumn. Widely planted in Hokkaido and central Honshu for timber.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {松|まつ}: pine — general term; pines keep their needles year-round
- {杉|すぎ}: Japanese cedar — Japan's most planted timber tree; evergreen
- {檜|ひのき}: Japanese cypress — prized for construction; evergreen
